driver: issue #43 (description compression to the amended §3.5 listing-budget target)
method: HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING §6.5 fan-out, menu variant per houseCARL PR #295: one fresh-context judge per eval query (Opus, HIGH reasoning effort, no tools), each shown ONLY its single query plus the full lettered menu of all 11 NEW descriptions (anonymized, under-test skill unflagged) plus NONE, forced single pick, reasoning before verdict; one Opus adjudicator per skill scored recall/specificity from the judges' reasoning per §6.5 step 4. Judge model deliberately upgraded from PR #295's sonnet-low (maintainer decision). Contamination guard: the live install was moved aside for the fan-out window so fresh judges carried no stale skill listing. Gates: recall >= 80%, specificity >= 50%. Scope limit of this measurement: judges saw the clean, full-text 11-entry menu, so the fan-out validates discriminability among the 11 descriptions - NOT routing survival under the listing-truncation pressure issue #43 describes; the post-merge /doctor budget check is the separate, remaining test of that.
description_measured: Place new items or NPCs into Requiem's world via houseCARL — enter them in the right leveled list, container, or encounter zone at the correct tier, riding the Reqtificator's leveled-list merge instead of overwriting Requiem's curated distribution. Use when modded loot, gear, or spawns never appear in game, or a dungeon needs de-leveling. Load before editing any list or container.
adjudicator_notes: No overrides needed — every judge's reasoning matched its verdict token. Recall (q1-q9): all nine routed to D, each explicitly separating distribution/placement (leveled lists, containers, encounter zones, Reqtificator merge) from record stat-balance neighbours (K weapons, B armor, F NPC, I race), citing D's named triggers ("modded loot/gear/spawns never appear in game", "de-leveling a dungeon"). Specificity (q10-q18): D was considered and explicitly rejected as a near-miss in q12 (SPID ini = runtime distributor, not record-level list edit), q14 ("hand-placed" quest reward bypasses distribution entirely — no list to enter), q15 (containers ≠ merchant gold/barter economy → G), q16 (Requiem-curated list entry ≠ reconciling two non-Requiem loot mods), and q18 (ESP-side placement ≠ in-game "where's good loot" advice). q10/q11/q13/q17 didn't reach D at all. Boundary language in D ("riding the Reqtificator's leveled-list merge", ESP override) is doing the discriminating work on the runtime-distributor (SPID/KID) and gameplay-advice distractors.
